title: Power of Attorney & Healthcare Directive Builder
learning_objectives: Select appropriate agents for financial and healthcare decisions
Understand scenarios with versus without incapacity protection documents
Create personal action plan for obtaining these documents
Recognize that these documents protect you while LIVING
description: Interactive planning tool for creating personal incapacity protection strategy, including healthcare proxy selection, financial POA agent selection, and comparison of scenarios with and without documents.
instructions: Work through healthcare directive planning framework
Select financial power of attorney agent using criteria tool
Compare scenarios showing outcomes with and without documents
Create action plan for obtaining documents in {{STATE_NAME}}
Identify conversations needed with potential agents

components.description: Person authorized to make medical decisions if you're incapacitated
selection_criteria: Trusts and respects your values and wishes
Emotionally strong enough to make difficult decisions (life support, treatment options)
Available and willing to serve in this role
Can advocate effectively with medical professionals
potential_candidates: Close friend who knows your values
components.important_note: You CAN name an unmarried partner—that's often the point of this document

questions: If permanently unconscious, do you want machines keeping you alive?
What quality of life would you find unacceptable?
How aggressive should treatment be if recovery is unlikely?
Do you want to be an organ donor?
Donation for transplant, research, or both?
Cultural practices that should be honored?

recipients: Hospital where you'd likely receive care
Keep copy with other important documents

steps.action: Have detailed conversation with healthcare proxy
topics: Discuss specific scenarios (coma, terminal illness, dementia)
Share religious/spiritual beliefs affecting medical care
Clarify that they should honor YOUR wishes, not what they would want

components.description: Person authorized to manage financial matters if you're incapacitated
selection_criteria: Available to act quickly if needed
considerations: Financial POA and healthcare proxy can be different people
Choose financial skills over family obligation
Consider requiring two agents to act jointly for major decisions (added protection)
Name successor agents if first choice cannot serve

options.description: Effective immediately upon signing; remains effective during incapacity
pros: Agent can act immediately in emergency
cons: Theoretically could be misused (though legal protections exist)
options.recommendation: Preferred by most attorneys—if you trust someone enough to name them, trust them with immediate authority

options.description: Only becomes effective when doctor certifies you're incapacitated
pros: No risk of use while you're capable
cons: Proving incapacity can be difficult and delay access
Could leave bills unpaid during certification period
options.recommendation: Sounds appealing but creates practical problems—most experts recommend durable

limitations_to_consider: Some people exclude real estate sales (require separate authorization)
Some limit gift-giving to prevent abuse
Can specify dollar limits for major transactions
Can require second signature for transactions over certain amount

scenario_comparisons.situation: Critically injured, unconscious for 3 weeks, uncertain recovery

healthcare.decision_maker: Named healthcare proxy (Jamie's partner Alex) makes decisions
healthcare.process: Doctors consult with Alex about treatment options
healthcare.timeline: Immediate authorization for all necessary care
healthcare.family_dynamics: Parents understand Alex has legal authority; minimal conflict

financial.bill_payment: Named financial agent (Jamie's sister) pays rent, car payment, insurance from Jamie's accounts
financial.timeline: Bills paid on time, credit score protected

with_documents.family_impact: Family focuses on Jamie's recovery, not legal battles; Jamie's wishes honored; financial stability maintained

healthcare.decision_maker: Family battles over who has authority
healthcare.process: Parents vs. partner argue about treatment decisions
healthcare.timeline: Hospital delays some treatments while determining who can consent
healthcare.family_dynamics: Estranged parents make decisions; partner has no legal standing despite 5-year relationship

financial.bill_payment: No one can access Jamie's accounts
financial.account_access: Family must petition court for conservatorship
financial.timeline: 2-3 months to get conservatorship; bills go unpaid
financial.cost: $5,000-8,000 in legal fees; eviction notice received; credit damaged

without_documents.family_impact: Family torn apart by legal conflicts; partner excluded despite relationship; financial disaster compounds medical trauma; by time conservatorship granted, damage done

cost_comparison.without_documents: $5,000-8,000 (conservatorship) + credit damage + eviction risk + family conflict

scenario_comparisons.situation: Severe stroke, partially paralyzed, speech impaired, long recovery ahead

with_documents.healthcare: Morgan (named healthcare proxy) coordinates with doctors, makes rehabilitation decisions, ensures Taylor's preferences honored
with_documents.financial: Morgan (named financial agent) pays bills, manages investments, handles insurance claims, maintains household
with_documents.legal_status: Morgan has full legal authority despite not being married
with_documents.recovery_support: Morgan can make quick decisions to support Taylor's recovery without legal obstacles

without_documents.healthcare: Taylor's parents (who disapprove of same-sex relationship) make all medical decisions; Morgan excluded from discussions
without_documents.financial: Parents petition for conservatorship; Morgan has no access despite shared household
without_documents.legal_status: Morgan is legal stranger despite 6-year relationship and shared life
without_documents.recovery_support: Morgan can't even get medical information; forbidden from visiting by parents; shared home at risk because Morgan can't access Taylor's portion of mortgage
without_documents.cost: $7,000+ conservatorship + relationship destroyed + Taylor's wishes ignored + potential loss of shared home

scenario_comparisons.key_lesson: For unmarried couples (including same-sex couples), these documents are CRITICAL—you have NO automatic legal standing without them

free_resources: {{STATE_NAME}} Bar Association: Free forms and instructions
{{STATE_NAME}} Department of Health: Healthcare directive forms
Local hospitals: Patient services often provide free forms and assistance
Legal aid clinics: Free assistance for qualifying individuals

key_takeaways: Healthcare directives and financial POAs protect you while LIVING—more immediately relevant than wills for young adults
At age 18, parents have NO automatic authority—you need documents regardless of family relationships
Unmarried couples (including same-sex couples) have NO legal standing without these documents—absolutely critical
Cost of documents ($200-400) is trivial compared to conservatorship ($5,000-8,000) and family conflict
Have detailed conversations with named agents BEFORE crisis—they need to know your wishes
In {{STATE_NAME}}, specific forms and requirements apply—use state-approved documents

reflection_questions.question: Who would you trust to make medical decisions aligned with your values?
Who would you trust to manage your finances responsibly if you couldn't?
What life support preferences do you have?
When will you complete these documents?
